steps.content: On a sunny afternoon, you follow Lamia into an Eastside residential neighborhood. It's one of Eastside's rare old neighborhoods, somewhat cluttered and dilapidated, but full of life.

Walking through the narrow alleyways, you pass by children who just got off school, middle-aged folks talking on their phones, and senior citizens with bags of groceries, before finally reaching an apartment building at the edge of the neighborhood.
While waiting for the elevator, you overhear the conversation of two residents chatting in front of their homes.

steps.speaker: Resident A
steps.content: Did you hear? The folks from 601 went to complain to the management yesterday!

steps.speaker: Resident B
steps.content: Oh, about what?

steps.speaker: Resident A
steps.content: About 602, of course! What else could it be about?

steps.speaker: Resident B
steps.content: Oh... as they should. We can hear those strange sounds even from the 8th floor, and the elevator reeks every time it passes by the 6th floor. Tsk tsk, I can only imagine what they must go through living on the same floor.

steps.speaker: Resident A
steps.content: I know, right? But it's no use complaining. The family in 602 is as creepy as hell. The useless management here is too chicken to do anything about them. All they do is keep saying the "relevant departments have been notified."

steps.speaker: Resident B
steps.content: Sigh. Now that you mention it, weren't they quite normal before? How did they end up like this?

steps.speaker: Resident A
steps.content: I think it's because they joined that... what is it called? The Thau-something Society? The popular one online that talks about the ocean. I was curious, so I searched them up.

steps.speaker: Resident B
steps.content: And?

steps.speaker: Resident A
steps.content: They're really something else! You won't believe this, but their Ocean Messenger has gray skin all over!

steps.speaker: Resident B
steps.content: ...! L-like her?
The stout man pats the lanky man on the shoulder and points at you guys. The latter can't help but shriek when he sees Lamia.

steps.speaker: Resident A
steps.content: Y-yeah... She's here to visit 602?!
At this point, Lamia glances back at them. The pair flees in terror, tugging on each other's arms.

steps.speaker: Resident B
steps.content: Shhh! Stop talking! She might make you insane, too... run run run!
As they flee, Lamia looks away and snickers disdainfully.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Uh huh.
Did you bring me here to meet your "Seafarers"?

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: That's right.

Ding——the elevator door opens. Lamia leads you to the unit directly across the hall. A thin layer of dust had accumulated on the shoe rack by the door, while the apartment number "602" hangs lopsided with no one to fix it.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Go and see for yourself, my righteous Chief.
Smiling, she twists the doorknob and gestures dramatically at you to enter.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Welcome to the place where dreams come true.
As soon as she opens the door, you're hit by the stench of rotting garbage fermenting for months in an airless environment.
The lights are turned off inside. The windows are closed and the curtains are tightly drawn. There are only a few faint rays of light leaking out from the seams where the fabric meets the floor.

You blink, struggling to take in the surroundings under the faint light—the dusty ground is littered with packaging bags and unidentifiable clutter, making it impossible for you to move around freely.
This place looks more like an abandoned ruin than a lived-in home.
You can't see your way clearly in the dark. You swat at the buzzing flies as you carefully tread over all the obstacles, but still end up kicking a coffee table.
The table's legs screech against the floor as the bottles and jars on top tumble to the ground. The clatter echoes loudly across the silent room, startling even yourself.
...Are you sure they're really still here?

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Have some patience. Look, don't you see someone coming?
Only then do you notice the rustling sounds from the next room. You look over and see a blurry figure approaching slowly.
When the figure gets up close, you see that it's a disheveled woman.
She's holding a tray of something you can't make out. Her face is grimy, and her hair and clothes are a mess. She practically looks like a zombie.
You stare at the strange woman nervously, ready to defend yourself. However, she passes by you as if you don't exist.
...She can't see me?

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: That's right. She only has her husband and daughter in her eyes. Follow her and keep observing.
You follow the woman across the living room to a bedroom. You peek inside curiously, but all you can see in the darkness is the outline of a small bed, where a middle-aged man is sitting.
She knocks on the door frame and enters with a smile.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: Have some tea I just made, dear.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.content: Oh, why did you do it yourself again? What do we have a cook and servants for? Just leave this kind of thing to them. Don't tire yourself out.
The man gets up from the bed, takes the tray from the woman and puts it on the desk beside him. Only then do you see what's on the tray...

The cup is filled with murky liquid that gives off a foul sour odor, and there seems to be something wriggling among the ancient food scraps in the plate. You quickly turn away, your stomach churning.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: Don't worry, I'm fine. It's my little hobby.
The woman seems to be quite receptive to the man's concern, and smiles in contentment.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Mommy! Do we have any of those lemon tarts I like?
The crisp voice of a child rings out from behind the man. Only then do you notice another person under the pile of blankets. You sneak over as they chat to take a look.
But what you see makes you gasp in horror...
An emaciated little girl with gaunt cheeks lies motionless on her back. She doesn't even have the strength to get up, but is still giggling non-stop as if she can't feel the pain.
In stark contrast to the bubbly vigor in her voice, you see a gravely ill child who has withered away before getting the chance to bloom.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: Of course we do. Mommy made them just for you. It's to reward my baby for being top of the class again.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Wow, all right! I'll make sure to be top of the class forever!

steps.speaker: Man
steps.content: Hahaha, it seems that I'm in for a treat thanks to my daughter.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: The lemon tarts are for our daughter, but this chocolate muffin is to celebrate your promotion, dear! If it weren't for your hard work, we wouldn't be able to live in such a luxurious house...
You watch as the family lives out their happy fantasy in the suffocating, bug-infested darkness. The absurd and disturbing contrast makes you break out in cold sweat.
Your incredulous frown seems to amuse Lamia. She opens up her arms as if presenting a masterpiece.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Their daughter's illness has no cure, but I helped them out. Look how happy they are now.
This isn't helping them.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Why isn't it? I never impose upon anyone. They were the ones who asked me to fulfill their wish at all costs. I just helped them to see what they wanted to see, and they are quite happy in their illusion.
But none of it's real.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: It's their own choice. Reality is too painful for them. They don't have the means or courage to solve their problems, so they seek comfort in fantasy. Aren't all human beings like this?
No, I don't think everyone's like that.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Ha, if you don't believe me, go ask them yourself.
Hmm...
Lamia grabs your hand, and the scene in front of you begins to distort.
When you come back to your senses again, you find yourself standing in a warm and lovely children's room.
The dilapidated ruins around you have disappeared without a trace, replaced by pink wallpaper, cartoon bedding, plush dolls, and spotless floors and table tops.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: Ah, if it isn't the Messenger! What brought you here all of a sudden?
You hear the woman's surprised gasp. She quickly goes forward and takes Lamia's hand.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: You should've told me you were coming. I didn't make any preparations...
Lamia pats the woman's hand with a smile.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: No need for such formalities, my dear Seafarer.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.content: O Messenger! We couldn't be happier to see you! Alas, if it weren't for you, those quack doctors would've killed my daughter... You are our family's great savior! W-we really don't know how to thank you!
The man leads his daughter over, beaming happily like his wife.

The little girl looks at you and Lamia in curiosity, her big round eyes sparkling and her cherub cheeks a healthy pink. She looks completely different from the gaunt, bedridden skeleton you saw just now.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Don't thank me. It's your sincerity that moved the soul of the deep sea. I simply helped to the best of my ability. I'm very glad to see how happy you are now.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.content: We're very happy indeed! We've never been happier in our lives!
The man hugs his wife and daughter tightly as he speaks.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: Yeah, our daughter is everything to us. We're willing to pay whatever cost to restore her health. Why, I'd gladly pay with my own life, let alone a small membership fee!

steps.speaker: Man
steps.content: Besides, whatever money we spend, we can earn back. I used to be a workaholic and neglected my family. When I finally realized it, it was too late... But fortunately, you gave me a second chance, O Messenger!

steps.speaker: Man
steps.content: Now my boss appreciates me more than ever. My workload has reduced, while my salary has more than doubled! Everything keeps getting better and better! I'm also trying to be a better husband and a better father.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: Our daughter is also doing great. Though she can be naughty at times, she's very smart and hardworking. After recovering and going back to school, she made a lot of new friends, and her teachers all praise her. She's our little angel and I'm so proud of her...

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Mommy! Can I go outside to play for a bit?
Either bashful from being praised or tired of hearing the adults banter, the girl tugs at her mother's sleeve and asks to leave.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: Of course. Just don't go too far.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: I'm off then... Bye Mommy and Daddy! Bye mister! Bye miss!
steps.female_content: I'm off then... Bye Mommy and Daddy! Bye ladies!

steps.content: Before leaving, the well-mannered little girl bids you goodbye. You smile and pat her head. The warm and realistic touch bewilders you.
The woman's eyes brim with tears as she watches her daughter skip into the distance.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: When I got the diagnosis from the hospital, I felt like I had been struck by a bolt of lightning. Terminal illness... We've all seen such things on TV, but who can imagine it happening to their own child?

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: She's only eleven. Her life is only beginning! Thank goodness she had the great fortune of meeting you, otherwise... What would she do? What would I do? I can't even begin to imagine...
Choking up again, she and her husband kneel down together and kowtow to Lamia.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: O merciful Ocean Messenger, you're our great savior!

Lamia proudly looks down at the kowtowing pair, as if relishing in some type of success. However, the gentle smile on her face soon vanishes. When she speaks again, there is no trace of warmth in her voice.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Sigh, but too bad, your happy days are coming to an end.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.content: W-what do you mean by that?
The couple gets up and looks at Lamia in confusion. Lamia shoots you a taunting look, making sure to enunciate every word:

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Someone asked me to come here to tell you the truth.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: ...The truth? What truth? I-I don't understand...
The woman follows Lamia's gaze and stares at you, visibly unnerved. Lamia wriggles her eyebrows at you, prompting you to take over the conversation.
You look at the scene around you, then turn your gaze back to the couple huddling together. Their fearful eyes make your heart heavy.
To shatter this piteous family's last hope and illusion, and throw them back into the heart-wrenching despair of reality, is indeed tougher and crueler than you had imagined.
You take a deep breath and finally muster up the courage to speak.
What you see around you is just an illusion. Your child's health is actually getting worse day by day. There is no cure. This is the truth.
After a long silence, the man lets out a dry laugh.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.content: Y-you must be joking... You saw for yourselves, she just went out to play... Sh-she's in good health now! She even won second place in her school race! How can she be...

steps.speaker: Man
steps.content: O Messenger... h-he's lying, isn't he?!
steps.female_content: O Messenger... sh-she's lying, isn't she?!

steps.content: He looks over at Lamia pleadingly, his tone becoming increasingly desperate. Lamia's answer, however, shatters his last bit of hope.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I'm sorry.
With a wave of her hand, you all return to the filthy apartment, where the emaciated, bedridden little girl is still struggling to breathe.

As the illusion disappears, the woman slumps to the ground, sobbing into her hands. The man also stumbles back in despair, leaning on a desk to stop himself from falling over. He lets out a low, hopeless chuckle.

steps.speaker: Man
steps.content: I knew it... How could it be so easy... How could we be so lucky... How could fate have spared us so easily?

steps.speaker: Man
steps.content: It's too late... It's too late after all...
Heavy sorrow and despair fills every inch of the room, making it hard for you to breathe.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: If I let you choose, will you choose to return to reality and live in pain, or for me to wipe your memory and let you keep on living in that happy illusion?

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: The illusion! Please wipe my memory and bring back the illusion! Please...
Lamia barely finishes her sentence before the woman yells out her reply without hesitation.
But hiding in that illusion won't really solve the problem.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: Then tell us, how do we solve our problem?! Who can solve it for us? Can you? Can you cure her?
You don't know what to reply. You know there's nothing you can do for them. But if someone really yearned for that illusion so much, they wouldn't be dragged back to reality with just one sentence.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: I know it's just a means of escape... But what's wrong with escaping forever? Reality is just too cruel. How can I keep on living without a shred of hope?

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: If I return to reality, I might be able to be with her in her last moments, but here, I have all the time in the world! In the illusion, I can be with her for decades, maybe even forever!

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: Here, I can watch her grow up, follow her dreams, and do whatever she wants. I can watch her find love, start a family, and have children of her own... I want to see her live a full life!
But... none of it's real...

steps.speaker: Man
steps.content: Who can say what's real and what's not?

steps.speaker: Man
steps.content: To us, the joy of this illusion is real enough. This is also my choice. We're too tired.
You fall silent. You know that no matter what you say, they won't change their decision.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I must say, as one of mankind's rare positive sides, "love" is indeed an incredible thing. It can make a person overcome their innate selfishness and give unconditionally to someone else.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: But you see, human beings will eventually be weakened, hurt and blinded by it, and consequently lose their minds. Like I said, everything will eventually descend into darkness.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Let's go. It's already clear who won.
Lamia starts to activate her power to leave the illusion, but you grab her hand.
There's still someone you haven't asked—the one who is the object of all this love. Her parents' choice is not necessarily her choice.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Ridiculous. Even her parents made this choice. You expect the suffering child herself to choose differently?
We won't know till you ask.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: You... really are the most stubborn person I've ever met. Fine, then. To beat you fair and square, I'll make sure that you have no illusions left whatsoever.
Your surroundings change again. You come to a garden, where the little girl is staring into the distance from a swaying swing. The scene is strangely melancholy.
Lamia walks up to the little girl confidently and asks her the same question.
The girl hesitates for a long time, then gives a surprising answer.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: I... I want to go back to reality.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: What!?
Lamia can't believe her ears. She grabs the girl by the shoulders somewhat hysterically.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Here, you can live a healthy and happy life, and do whatever you want. If you go back to reality, you'll be in constant pain and suffering. You won't be able to run around freely, or even get a good night's sleep...

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Have you forgotten what that's like?!

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: This cruel and unjust world tormented you so much for no reason. It robbed you of the life you should've had. Why would you want to go back?!
The girl flinches, but still looks courageously into Lamia's eyes.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Because of Mommy and Daddy.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: They can be with you in the illusion forever.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: But they're trying to find a way to cure me. They want me to be cured for real.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Don't you understand? You can't be cured! Your life is over!
Lamia...
You want to stop her. It's unbearably cruel to tell a child this ugly truth, but the girl just nods and accepts it calmly.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Life will be over for me soon, but not for Mommy and Daddy. I want to tell them I love them. I want them to start a new life...

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: That way, they can live well even outside the illusion. And I would feel... relieved.
The illusion cracks and collapses before your eyes, shattering into dust before vanishing without a trace.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: How... how could this be... how is this possible...
Lamia stands alone amidst the debris. It's the first time you see true vulnerability and confusion in her eyes.
You walk over and put a gentle hand over her shoulder.

I can't deny that there's more darkness than light in this world. I know that in their powerlessness, most will choose to flee, compromise, or succumb to the darkness when faced with the cruel reality of life.

Yet at the same time, there will always be those who refuse to give up the light, no matter how mired they are. They choose to face and overcome their pain. That's why these glimmers of light in the dark are so precious.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: They choose to...
She chuckles bitterly.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: But what about me? All this time, when did I ever get the chance to choose?

options: You have a chance right now.

choices.text: You have a chance right now.

steps.content: You can choose to bid farewell to the past, let go of your prejudices, and see yourself and the world in a new light.
I've never condemned your way of life. I truly think that you're amazing to have survived such a depressing and hopeless world.
I know most people can't even begin to imagine how much you've suffered, but don't let that make you embrace the darkness and turn your back on the light.

You've never been a freak. Being special is not a bad thing. It means that you're unique. You deserve love, acceptance and admiration. At least when you're with me, in the MBCC, you can let go of all your masks and be your true self.
Lamia falls silent. You know it'll be a long, arduous journey to fully change her views, but at least you're taking the first step together.
The little girl wakes up. She grabs the corner of Lamia's shirt and smiles weakly but earnestly.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Thank you for granting my wish and bringing us back to reality, miss.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: I didn't get to tell you in the illusion just now, but I think you're really cool and pretty. If I got the chance to grow up, I'd want to be just like you.
You open the heavy curtains. The afterglow of the setting sun instantly disperses the darkness, filling every corner of the room.
There is a lot of dust and grime on the windows, but the warm golden light shines through them, gently illuminating Lamia.
Lamia stands next to the girl's bed, clasping her hands in genuine reverence.
It's as if the sunlight had finally reached the depths of the ocean.
